A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the Prism Hypothesis and Unified Autoencoding, with substantial revisions to the method and experiments. All 11 pages of v2 and 12 pages of v3 support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both end with references.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction, generation, linear-probing, spectral-analysis and ablation results in Figures 2–6 and Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v3 reports original reconstruction and generation results, semantic-loss and masking ablations, convergence and efficiency measurements, and controlled JIT comparisons.

M1.justification: v2's FFT band projector, iterative residual splitting, Gaussian noise injection and convolutional spectral fusion are replaced by channel-wise DCT, zig-zag coefficient ordering, high-frequency zero masking and inverse-DCT decoding. v3 also explicitly develops spatial-domain and frequency-domain generative procedures. The low-frequency semantic-alignment objective remains.

E1.justification: ImageNet-1K/MS-COCO reconstruction and ImageNet generation remain; additional encoders and pixel-space modeling alone do not establish new task coverage. Retrieval-scenario coverage is ambiguous: v2 reports low- and high-pass evaluations, whereas v3 Section 3.1 and Figure 3 report only low-pass evaluations, but the retained caption still asserts high-pass degradation. It is unclear whether that scenario was removed or only its quantitative display omitted.

E2.justification: Reconstruction Table 1 adds SD-VAE variants, VA-VAE and SVG, while removing TokenFlow, DualViTok, EMU2, UniLIP and the explicitly named SD-VAE-EMA row. Generation Table 2 adds SiT and SVG and removes VAR. v3 also introduces the JIT comparison and removes v2's standalone linear-probing comparison against VFMTok, BEiT, MAE, MAGE and other baselines.

E3.justification: Training changes from three stages to two, with adversarial training introduced during the frozen-encoder stage. Semantic alignment changes from one base band to specified token fractions. Retrieval changes from Recall@5 to Recall@1, and spectral analysis changes from averaged magnitudes to squared DCT-coefficient energy. Added spatial/frequency and JIT experiments introduce token-budget and matched-model controls, including 700M-parameter, patch-size-32 JIT comparisons.

E4.justification: v2's component-addition, band-count and Band0-versus-concatenation ablations, plus its t-SNE analysis, disappear. v3 instead tests semantic-alignment fractions and masking ratios, measures convergence and computational efficiency, and compares encoder spectra before and after unified training. The retrieval analysis is also revised, with the plotted high-pass comparison removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or defined uncertainty estimates. Both present point estimates and curves without uncertainty bands.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes UAE-DINOv2-B ImageNet PSNR/SSIM/rFID from 29.65/0.88/0.19 to 32.17/0.92/0.35. Table 2 changes UAE gFID/IS from 1.68/301.6 to 1.52/234.5. These accompany method and protocol revisions, so they are not controlled cross-version gains. Numerous entries are added or removed, including v3's matched 80-epoch JIT comparison: FID 16.06 versus 14.55 and IS 123.30 versus 132.57 for JIT versus UAE(JIT).

T1.justification: The formal representation changes substantially: v2's residual-projection recurrences, stochastic corruption and residual-fusion definitions are replaced by DCT coefficients, radial-frequency and ordered-token definitions, and a zero-masking formulation. The original low/high-pass formalization and semantic-alignment loss remain. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central spectral hypothesis and semantic/pixel unification claim remain. However, v3 elevates effectiveness in both latent and pixel spaces to a main contribution, explicitly claiming faster convergence and improved FID/IS when integrated with JIT in the abstract, introduction and conclusion. This substantially broadens the claimed applicability beyond v2's tokenizer-focused contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of the semantic-preservation versus reconstruction tradeoff, masking as a source of stronger structural priors, spectral-energy redistribution after unified training, and faster generation through compact frequency representations. These replace v2's emphasis on band-count robustness and the classification advantage of Band0. Pixel-space applicability is also newly argued.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies AdamW, learning-rate schedules, 16-epoch first-stage training, discriminator/generator activation epochs, masking and alignment fractions, latent shapes, and a 1400-epoch progressive SiT schedule. These materially expand implementation documentation without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. Conversely, v2's explicit training/evaluation split statement and 30-epoch SGD linear-probing recipe disappear. The code-access URL remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to JIT, SiT, DCTdiff, SDXL and SigLIP2, including a short positioning statement about DCT-based pixel generation. References associated with removed comparisons or the former flow-based motivation, including Glow, MAE and MAGE, disappear. The broader positioning around unified tokenizers and spectral representations remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The methodology is extensively rewritten and reorganized: separate residual-splitting, modulation and semantic-loss sections become an integrated autoencoder description followed by generative modeling. The standalone semantic-understanding section disappears, and the three-part ablation section becomes a six-part discussion. Preliminary verification and implementation explanations are substantially expanded.

P2.justification: The architecture diagram is redrawn, and v3 adds a spatial-versus-frequency modeling diagram, convergence plots and a before/after spectral plot. The retrieval and encoder-spectrum plots are redesigned, the reconstruction montage uses new examples and additional encoder variants, and the t-SNE figure is removed. Tables are substantially restructured, including moving probing results into reconstruction Table 1 and adding efficiency and JIT displays.

improvement.justification: v3 provides useful implementation schedules, targeted ablations, efficiency evidence and controlled JIT results. However, it loses the explicit probing protocol and introduces conflicts in central results: v2 Table 2 and Section 4.3 agreed on 1.68/301.6, while v3's table reports 1.52/234.5 but its prose retains the old values. v3 Section 4.2 also gives DINOv2-B PSNR as 31.00 although Table 1 reports 32.17. These gains in documentation and evidence coexist with material losses in reporting consistency, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
